title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion

claims.statement: Diffusion Policy conditions action generation on recent observations, predicts an action sequence over Tp steps, executes Ta steps, then replans; To denotes the observation horizon.
claims.scope: Receding-horizon policy formulation; this does not establish arbitrary long-horizon task success.

claims.statement: For its real-world experiments the paper reports DDIM inference with 100 training denoising iterations and 10 inference iterations, giving 0.1 seconds of inference latency on an Nvidia 3080 GPU.
claims.scope: Reported inference setup and hardware; latency is not a universal end-to-end robot control rate.

claims.statement: In visual Transport with proficient-human demonstrations, DiffusionPolicy-C scores 1.00/0.93 and LSTM-GMM 0.88/0.62. Each pair is best checkpoint versus last-ten-checkpoint average, aggregated over three training seeds and 50 environment initializations.
claims.locator: Table II Transport ph; Table I caption and Section V.B on page 7
claims.scope: Simulation, visual observations, proficient-human demonstrations, success rates. These are not state-policy, multi-human, or physical-robot results.
